Open • FLYBYME (Tim) opened less than a minute ago • 0 comments
Labels: bug


  Two problems, and the second is why adding a second machine made things     
  worse                                                                       
  rather than better.                                                         
                                                                              
  --------                                                                    
                                                                              
  ## 1. Every node but the target reports running nothing                     
                                                                              
   src/fleet/methods/node.ts , building the fleet summary:                    
                                                                              
    runningServices: host === targetHostname ? runningServices : [],          
    provisionedServices: host === targetHostname ? provisionedServices : [],  
                                                                              
  One Supervisor is queried — the target's. Every other machine is reported as
  running nothing, and the fleet console draws exactly that:                  
                                                                              
    ● surf.surfdns.net    running=[]                                          
    ● ubuntu-GW15-43P     running=[api identity fleet supervisor catalog      
  builder cdn]                                                                
                                                                              
  surf was running three services. Reported as connected and empty, which     
  reads as                                                                    
  a machine that joined and failed to start anything — the exact confusion    
  this                                                                        
  console exists to end. Reported as: "i see that surf is connected but i cant
  load anything into it."                                                     
                                                                              
  Query each connected node's Supervisor. One slow or wedged machine must not 
  stall the whole report — the same rule  node_reconcile  already follows:    
  gather                                                                      
  what you can, and say per node what you could not.                          
                                                                              
  A node that does not answer is  connected: true  with an unknown observed   
  state,                                                                      
  and that must be visibly different from  running: [] . "I could not ask" and
  "it is running nothing" are opposite diagnoses.                             
                                                                              
  --------                                                                    
                                                                              
  ## 2. Nothing decides where work runs                                       
                                                                              
   builder.build_start  round-robins across every node that mounts  builder . 
  After surf joined, half the builds landed on a 981MB VPS in Chicago, across 
  a                                                                           
  home internet link instead of the 32GB laptop three feet away. A deploy that
  took two minutes stopped finishing at all, and the mesh link dropped        
  underneath                                                                  
  it:                                                                         
                                                                              
    Peer disconnected: surf.surfdns.net                                       
    Max reconnection attempts reached                                         
                                                                              
  Both machines mount  builder , so both are equally eligible. Nothing        
  anywhere                                                                    
  says a build wants memory, or that a node across the internet is a worse    
  choice                                                                      
  than one holding the blobs already.                                         
                                                                              
  This is placement, and it has been on the design list since the start. From 
  the surfdns notes: "Placement becomes a first-class attribute."             
                                                                              
  What it needs, at minimum:                                                  
                                                                              
  • a service can declare what it wants — memory, and whether it should prefer
  the node that already holds the data                                        
  • a caller can express prefer local for work that is cheap locally and      
  expensive remotely, which is every build                                    
  • a node can decline work it cannot do, rather than accepting and timing out
                                                                              
  A timeout is the worst possible signal here and it is what we have now: no  
  error, no fallback, no indication which machine took the job. The immediate 
  mitigation is to take  builder  out of the  serve  group so surf stops      
  offering                                                                    
  it — that is a workaround, and this issue is the fix.                       
                                                                              
  Do not build a scheduler. The smallest thing that stops a 981MB box in      
  another                                                                     
  country being treated as interchangeable with the machine holding the       
  artifacts.                                                                  


View this issue on GitHub: https://github.com/FLYBYME/surfdns/issues/53

### Unreachable Node Status Representation

An unreachable or failing node now presents in `node.status` output as:

```json
{
  "hostname": "failing-host",
  "connected": true,
  "runningServices": [],
  "provisionedServices": [],
  "error": "Supervisor query timed out after 3000ms"
}
```

This clearly distinguishes unreachable nodes from offline nodes (`connected: false`) and reachable nodes with no running services (`connected: true`, `runningServices: []`, no `error`).
